scope: Read-only source inspection during unchanged matched evaluation; no runtime timing instrumentation added
findings: Newest RGB frame and asynchronous YOLO feature age are different quantities.
Policy chooses action from prior returned observation before guarded env.step captures and classifies a newer screenshot.
Guard screenshot is not repacked into the already chosen policy action.
Legacy frame_age_at_command_ms uses last_capture_end after guard capture, so it does not measure original policy-observation age.
last_capture_end is stamped after menu scoring/compatibility resize, not at desktop present time.
5 ms requested key hold does not measure browser dispatch or Unity input-to-visible-response latency.
Four-frame stack provides temporal context, but does not guarantee motion anticipation is learned.
Actor-only BC freezes the visual/aux extractor; PPO continuation can update the policy feature extractor.
Training-only four-frame post-resume refresh passively waits while game is running; supplied overnight traces show roughly 213-277 ms to fourth accepted frame.
100-episode evaluation caps episodes at 15 seconds, and therefore does not validate sustained later high-speed play.
recommended_measurement: Preserve timestamps/IDs for the exact frame stack used by policy.
Measure policy inference, guard duration and keydown dispatch; report median/p95/p99 for policy-frame-to-key.
Correlate commanded actions with browser receipt and visible Unity movement before treating delivery as confirmed.
Compare detector source age separately from RGB age and measure post-optimizer first-action delay.
Only then A/B one performance setting at a time on the same checkpoint, without weakening guards.
inference: Existing system plausibly supports substantially better play, but adequacy at high speed and a more-steps-only explanation are not established.
